subject: general
question: With which of the following organisations were Ram Prasad Bismil, Chandrashekhar Azad and Bhagat Singh associated?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Hindustan Socialist Republican Association**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Hindustan Socialist Republican Association** (HSRA) was a revolutionary organization that aimed to overthrow British rule in India.
 
• Prominent freedom fighters such as **Ram Prasad Bismil, Chandrashekhar Azad, and Bhagat Singh** were associated with this organization.
 
• The HSRA was founded in 1928, following the reorganization of the Hindustan Republican Association (HRA).
 
• The organization was known for its radical approach, including armed struggle and acts of violence against British officials.
 
• It played a significant role in inspiring young Indians to join the freedom movement and fight for independence.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The **HSRA** was initially formed as the Hindustan Republican Association (HRA) in 1924 by revolutionaries like **Ram Prasad Bismil, Ashfaqulla Khan, and Sachindra Nath Sanyal**.
 
• In 1928, the HRA was reorganized and renamed HSRA to emphasize its socialist orientation and commitment to achieving independence through revolutionary means.
 
• One of the most notable actions of HSRA was the **Kakori Train Robbery** in 1925, which aimed to fund their activities by stealing money from the British government.
 
• Bhagat Singh, a key member of the HSRA, is remembered for his role in the **Lahore Conspiracy Case** and his execution in 1931, which galvanized the Indian independence movement.
 
• The legacy of HSRA continues to inspire contemporary movements and the youth of India in their pursuit of justice and freedom.
